In an effort to help myself deal with the hiatus (still not sure how much of that year and a half is left) and also to contribute something original for once, here's a theory that I've been playing around with for the last few days.

This is my attempt to explain some of Rick's behavior. I can't prove any of this, I'm just connecting what dots I see.

Over the series' run, Rick regularly breaks the fourth wall. We see him...

  • Tell Morty about all the future adventures they would have.
  • Mention www.rickandmorty.com.
  • Ask Nintendo for free stuff.
  • Address the audience directly.

He even goes so far as breaking the fifth(?) wall, where he's literally a mouthpiece for the writers' thoughts. In Interdimensional Cable 2, he tells the nurse he's doing "a sequel" when she demands to know what he's up to. This demonstrates that not only does Rick know that people are watching, but that individual segments of his and Morty's lives are 'episodes'.

So I'd say it's fairly safe to assume that Rick knows that he's on a TV show. Considering the cable box lets you watch things from infinite dimensions, that means eventually he would find channels where he's the star. Now... Does Rick know this for sure, or is it just an educated guess? Theoretically he knows that they exist, but we can't be sure if he's ever actually come across one. However, his general disdain for Beth and Jerry when all they want to do is watch their other lives makes me think that he's either done it himself at some point, or he's disgusted by the thought of doing something that egotistical.

But infinite dimensions really are a bitch, huh? That means every television show from every reality also exists as it's own reality. There's even an issue of the Rick and Morty comics that takes place in the Ball Fondlers reality. In other words, we exist in a reality where Rick and Morty is a cartoon show that we watch for entertainment. Rick and Morty exist in a reality where they're real and Ball Fondlers is a show they watch for entertainment. And then of course there's the best reality, where Ball Fondlers is real.

So the question is - are the writers from our reality narrating Rick's and Morty's (and Summer's, and Beth's, and Jerry's....) lives, or are Rick and Morty acting out our writers' narration? It's a question of causality. Which causes which? Chicken, or the egg?

Could this be the crushing existential question at the core of Rick's character? Wisecrack's The Philosophy of Rick and Morty discusses Rick's flip-flopping between passive and active nihilism, which I'll call Sad Rick and Angry Rick.

Angry Rick is the Rick who becomes an interdimensional fugitive. Angry Rick hates government. Angry Rick blows up Zigerian scammers and gets into fistfights with Zeep Xanflorp. Angry Rick shouts "Yes! Fuck you, God! Not today, bitch!" Angry Rick is who Rick is as an active nihilist. Angry Rick seeks to introduce entropy into the system. Angry Rick is Rick's rebellion against God, the writers, his father - he seems to really have a problem with his father - or whatever being might be responsible for his existence. Angry Rick is mirrored by Zeep Xanflorp's hatred for Rick ("I didn't ask to be born!!").

Sad Rick is the Rick who abandons his family to do drugs with an entire planet. Sad Rick sells weapons to killers so he can go to Blips and Chitz and play a game that is literally someone else's life all day. Sad Rick is an alcoholic. Sad Rick says "I'm okay with this. Be good, Morty. Be better than me." and "Yeah, join the club." Sad Rick is the Rick who tries to kill himself. Sad Rick believes that nothing matters, PERIOD. Sad Rick is dominant when Rick allows himself to be crushed by the thought of only existing as someone else's entertainment. Sad Rick is end of S2 Rick.

And finally, rarest of all, is Happy Rick. Happy Rick is the Rick who doesn't care about just how insignificant life is. If there is no big picture, that means anything can be meaningful if it's meaningful to you. Happy Rick doesn't say "Wubba lubba dub dub!"

So, after all that, we can see why the key to (Rick's) happiness is don't think about it.

That got a lot longer than I meant it to, but yeah.
